2. The petitioner's case in short, is that he along with respondent Nos. 5-8 contested the election for the office of the chairman of No-13 Bathgaon Union Parishad under Upazila Chhatak in the district of Sum. The election was held on 10.2.88 in all the polling stations fairly and peacefully but pollings at Mandalpur Primary School Centre and Zikli High School polling Stations were interrupted and went beyond the control of the presiding Officer and as a result of which pollings in these two centres were stopped and declared adjourned by the presiding officers. Thereafter fresh polls were held on 13.4.88 at Zikli High School and Mandalpur primary school polling stations. Poll in Zikli High School polling station held peacefully but pollings at Mandail primary School polling stations were again interrupted and obstructed due to violence created by respondent no. 5 and his men. The Presiding Officer stopped the poll at about 12 in the noon and issued a certificate to the petitioner to the effect. It is stated by the petitioner that after the poll being declared adjourned, the Presiding Officer along with other personnels with election materials left the polling station for Chhatak Upazila Headquarter. The petitioner and respondent No.5 and 7 and other member candidates also followed him and the Presiding Officer went to his residence and other contesting candidates departed. Thereafter the petitioner reaching at Chhatak Upazila Head-quarter tried to inform the Presiding Officer about the happenings at Mandalpur primary School Polling Station but he refused to hear him. The petitioner thereafter went to Upazilla Nirbahi Officer and informed him about the situation in writing. On the following morning namely on 14.4.88 the petitioner came to know that the Presiding Officer had submitted a result sheet to the Returning Officer. The petitioner finding that his complaint was not being heeded to, filed a review petition on 19.4.88 before the Election Commission praying for repolling in Mandalpur Primary School Station and the said Commission ordered for an inquiry into the matter by the District Election Officer who submitted his report on 25.5.88. 

 4. Respondent No. 5 Anwar Hossain Chowdhury has appeared and shown cause by filing an affidavit-in opposition denying the allegations of the petitioner made in the petition and asserted that the allegations are false, concocted and fabricated and that election at Mandalpur Primary School Polling station held peacefully without any interruption or obstruction and that the result sheet as submitted by the presiding officer was done in course of his normal official business. He terms the Certificate issued by the Presiding Officer to the petitioner (Annexure-A) as a concocted fabricated and ante-dated paper obtained by exercising undue influence or for illegal gain for the purpose of this case. He asserts that no such certificate was ever issued by the presiding officer to the petitioner. He empathetically denies that there occurred no such disturbance at Mandalpur Primary School polling station or that pollings was adjourned on 13.4.88. He asserts that the result sheet was submitted to the Returning officer and the (respondent No. 5) was declared elected and his name was also sent for publication in the Official Gazette. He denies the allegation of the petitioner as false, concocted and malafide. 

 6. Mr. Miftahuddin Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.5, on the other hand, argues that the temcomporary cessation of pollings at Mandalpur Primary School polling Centre was not a ground for stopping the election and that the presiding Officer was completely within his jurisdiction in resuming the election after a short while and completing the pollings in due course of time. He submits that a temporary suspension of election does not bring the case of the petitioner within the mischief of Rule 29(1) of the Union Parishad (Election) Rules, 1983 and as such is not violative of that rule. 

 8. Of course from Annexure 'G' series and also Annexures 2 and 3 of the Affidavit-in-Opposition it appears that polling at Mandalpur Primary School Polling Station was suspended from 12 to 12.30 in the noon and thereafter pollings resumed and continued upto 5.30 P.M. and thereafter presiding Officer closed down the election when there was no voters left in the enclosure as per Rules. Now the whole question centres round only one point, namely whether this suspension of election from 12 to 12.30 in the noon would at all bring the case of the petitioner within the mischief of Rule 29(1) of the Election Rules or not. Rule 29(1) of the Union Parishad (Election) Rules runs as follows: 

 10. The word 'stop' means 'to bring an end to' or close up. It appears from the facts and circumstances of the case that there occurred disturbance for a short while and there-after pollings resumed. It is Blear from the Annexure annexed to the petition as we 11 as the affidavit-in-opposition that the Presiding Officer did not close down the pollings after 12.30 on 13.4.88; rather from 12.30 he resumed the election and closed down the same at 5.30 P.M. The Presiding Officer was not satisfied that the circumstances available were enough to warrant closing down the pollings at that centre. Rather when circumstance/situation became calm and quiet and became congenial for resumption of election, he resumed the pollings after 12.30 and closed it down at 5.30 when all the voters who were within the enclosure cast their votes. Therefore the word stoppage to bring an end to did not operate at 12.30 when the pollings were suspended. 

 11. Therefore the expression "for reasons beyond the control" means the circumstances which go beyond the control of the presiding Officer and threaten to effect or destroy the panctitity of the election by violating the principle "Just honest and fair" election. And Rule 29(1) then and there only app lies. But in the cases where somehow some sort of sudden temporary broil, dissensions or disruption break out and pollings are haulted causing no prejudice to parties or the process of election and the situation is within the control of the Presiding Officer, Rule 29(1) certainly does not apply. Mere haulting of pollings may also take place if voters do not turn up but process of election goes on, Even infringement of any Rule cannot vitiate the election unless the same has materially affected the results thereof.
